sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Global Hydrological Balance**: Oceans hold roughly **96.5%** of global water, driving the atmospheric water cycle via evaporation and precipitation.
• **Blue Economy Paradigm**: Sustainable use of ocean resources for economic growth, improved livelihoods, and jobs while preserving ocean ecosystem health.
• **Thermal Energy Reservoir**: Oceans absorb over **90%** of excess anthropogenic heat, acting as the primary climate regulator.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends up to **200 nautical miles** from the baseline under UNCLOS, granting sovereign rights over natural resources.

items.definition: A sea zone prescribed by UNCLOS over which a state has special rights regarding the exploration and use of marine resources, stretching up to 200 nautical miles from its coast.
Porous potato-sized lumps strewn across abyssal plains containing nickel, copper, cobalt, and manganese, targeted by India's Deep Ocean Mission.
An autonomous international organization established under UNCLOS to organize and control mineral-resource-related activities in the international seabed area beyond national jurisdiction.
India's flagship initiative launched by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) to develop deep-sea technologies for mining minerals and exploring deep-sea biodiversity.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Central Indian Ocean Basin (CIOB)**: Allocated to India by the ISA for polymetallic nodule exploration, located roughly 2,000 km south of the Indian mainland.
• **Coastal Desalination Hubs**: Concentrated in water-scarce metropolitan regions like Chennai (Nemmeli and Minjur plants), Gujarat coast, and Gulf nations leveraging thermal MSF technology.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: High capital expenditure for deep-sea mining, brine toxicity from desalination plants impacting coastal ecology, and unregulated marine plastic pollution.
• **Policy Interventions**: Deep Ocean Mission funding, Blue Economy policy framework, adherence to UN Sustainable Development Goal 14 (Life Below Water).

items.title: Mnemonic for UNCLOS Maritime Zones (Increasing Distance from Baseline)
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: **T**he **C**oast **E**njoys **H**igh-seas (**T**CCEH)
• **Decoded Meaning**: **T**erritorial Sea (12 nm) -> **C**ontiguous Zone (24 nm) -> **E**xclusive Economic Zone (200 nm) -> **H**igh Seas (Beyond 200 nm).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly prevents confusion regarding jurisdiction limits and sovereign rights in UPSC matching questions.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember **'200 for Wealth, 12 for Health'** — 200 nautical miles for economic resource rights (EEZ), and 12 nautical miles for complete territorial sovereignty.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that coastal nations have absolute sovereignty over their EEZ. This is incorrect; states only have sovereign rights for exploring and exploiting natural resources, while freedom of navigation and overflight applies to all nations in the EEZ.
Mains Value Addition: Quote the 'Blue Economy' as a vital engine for India's $5 trillion economy goal, linking it to maritime security (SAGAR doctrine) and climate resilience.

keyTakeaways: Oceans represent critical stores of biological, mineral, and energy resources governed internationally by UNCLOS.
India's Deep Ocean Mission and EEZ rights provide strategic leverage for critical mineral security and technological self-reliance.
Balancing resource extraction with marine ecological conservation is paramount for sustainable development under SDG 14.
